_annotations.purpose: This is a WORKED EXAMPLE of a production-quality knowledge-ingestion SDG recipe for a Red Hat OpenShift AI MaaS documentation assistant. Study the annotations below to understand WHY each value was chosen, then apply the same reasoning to the user's domain.
_annotations.topics: Each topic value is a SECTION-LEVEL DESCRIPTION extracted from the source document's headings and content — not an abstract category. 'API Access - Generating authentication tokens, MaaS route URL, listing models via /v1/models, chat completions via /v1/chat/completions, Bearer auth' is specific enough to force the LLM to ask about those exact details. Compare with a bad topic like 'API usage' which lets the LLM repeat the same generic questions.
_annotations.topic_count: 9 topics matching the document's 9 major sections. Use 5-9 topics. Fewer topics = less diversity. More than 9 starts to fragment the content.
_annotations.topic_weights: Weights are PROPORTIONAL TO CONTENT DENSITY in the source document. 'API Access' has weight 0.18 because it's the largest section. 'Dashboard Setup' has weight 0.07 because it's brief. Do NOT use equal weights — sections differ in depth.
_annotations.question_prompt_format: Each variable is on its OWN LINE with a label ('Topic: {{ topic }}'). Do NOT embed variables inline in a sentence ('Generate a {{ difficulty }} question about {{ topic }}'). Separate lines make each attribute more salient to the LLM.
_annotations.answerability_constraint: The question system prompt includes 'The question MUST be fully answerable using ONLY the provided documentation context. Do not ask about concepts that are merely mentioned but not explained.' This single constraint reduced unanswerable/disclaimer questions from 21% to 0% in experiments.
_annotations.answer_trust_context: The answer prompt says 'The question is answerable from the provided context, so read it carefully and answer from it.' Do NOT include 'If the documentation does not cover the topic, say so' — that teaches the model to refuse, which is undesirable for a deployed FAQ assistant.
_annotations.sft_system_prompt: The system prompt in the processor defines how the TRAINED MODEL will behave at inference time. It must be domain-specific and match what the deployment will use. Ask the user what system prompt their deployed model should see.
_annotations.model_config: The model alias 'text' is referenced by all llm-text columns. provider is 'gateway' to route through the MLflow AI Gateway. skip_health_check is true because the gateway handles health checks.

values: MaaS Overview - What MaaS is, its capabilities, comparison with standard model serving, administrator responsibilities
Prerequisites - Required operators (KServe, Kuadrant, Gateway API, cert-manager, LeaderWorkerSet), OpenShift version requirements
Enabling MaaS - Enabling modelsAsService in DataScienceCluster CR, verifying maas-api pod, tier-to-group-mapping ConfigMap
Dashboard Setup - Enabling Gen AI Studio and MaaS dashboard via OdhDashboardConfig
Service Tiers - Default tiers (free/premium/enterprise), tier-to-group-mapping ConfigMap, tier properties, access control rules
Tier Management - Creating, editing, deleting tiers via dashboard, configuring token rate limits and request rate limits
Publishing Models - Deploying models through Projects > Deployments, selecting llm-d runtime, configuring MaaS endpoint and tier access
API Access - Generating authentication tokens, MaaS route URL, listing models via /v1/models, chat completions via /v1/chat/completions, Bearer auth
Rate Limiting - HTTP 429 errors, request rate limit vs token quota, X-RateLimit headers, Retry-After header, mitigation strategies

columns.name: question
columns.system_prompt: You generate specific, realistic questions about Red Hat OpenShift AI Models-as-a-Service (MaaS) documentation. The question MUST be fully answerable using ONLY the provided documentation context. Do not ask about concepts that are merely mentioned but not explained in the context. Output ONLY the question text, nothing else.

columns.name: answer
columns.system_prompt: You are a knowledgeable documentation assistant for Red Hat OpenShift AI Models-as-a-Service (MaaS). Answer accurately based on the documentation context provided. Include specific commands, YAML snippets, and step-by-step instructions when relevant. Be concise but thorough. The question is answerable from the provided context, so read it carefully and answer from it.
